title: Canary weight oscillation leading to rollback deadlock during multi-region rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a controlled multi-region model rollout we observed rapid oscillation of canary traffic weights across regions which triggered the rollout controller to repeatedly attempt rollbacks. The controller eventually hit an internal deadlock because the rollback path required capacity in a region that had already been temporarily pinned to the new variant, preventing progress and causing elevated latency and 5xx spikes for impacted customers.
summary: Canary weight adjustment logic interacted poorly with multi-region promotion gating and capacity checks. Oscillation between weight schedules caused the rollout controller to re-enqueue conflicting rollback/promote operations and ultimately a deadlock when a capacity-based precondition could not be satisfied.
impact: Approximately 12 minutes of elevated 95th percentile latency for chat and generation routes in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. ~82 customers experienced degraded responses; three customers with SLO monitoring received alerts. No data exfiltration or model correctness regression detected.
timeline:
2026-03-11T09:02Z - Canary rollout started to eu-west-1 and us-east-1
2026-03-11T09:05Z - Observability alert: sudden increase in request latencies for canary routes (dashboards/realtime)
2026-03-11T09:07Z - Automated weight adjustment recommender bumped canary weight down in eu-west-1 due to latency
2026-03-11T09:08Z - Controller job in us-east-1 attempted to promote to higher weight following success signals -> weight bumped up
2026-03-11T09:09Z - Weight oscillation begins as both region controllers act on slightly out-of-sync health signals
2026-03-11T09:12Z - Rollback triggered in eu-west-1; controller attempts to provision capacity in fallback pool but pool is transiently pinned to canary variant by another promotion job
2026-03-11T09:15Z - Deadlock detected: rollback job waiting for capacity release, promotion job retrying, both holding soft locks
2026-03-11T09:20Z - Operators engaged (oncall/runtime-core). Manual intervention to force release of temporary pins and restart controllers
2026-03-11T09:23Z - Controllers reconcile, weight stabilized, latencies return to normal by 09:27Z
2026-03-11T09:30Z - Post-incident triage started
root_cause: Race conditions between independent regional rollout controllers and the cross-region capacity/pinning mechanism. Two controllers made contradictory weight changes based on slightly different signal windows. The pinning logic takes a short-exclusive lock but did not prevent concurrent promote/rollback attempts across regions, which allowed both operations to acquire overlapping soft locks and cause a deadlock when capacity preconditions could not be satisfied.
contributing_factors: 1) Health signals use 10s smoothing windows per-region leading to inconsistent views. 2) The rollout controller retry logic did not include global coordination when multi-region is enabled. 3) The pinning mechanism holds soft pins tied to jobs but lacks a lease expiration and global arbitration. 4) No automatic deadlock detection for controller job queues or pin-holder cycles.
detection_and_response: Detected by automated latency SLO alerting (console route-level 95th > threshold). Oncall flowed through runbook: initial rollback attempt, then escalated to runtime-core. Manual unpin and controller restart resolved the deadlock. Teams used the rollout debug endpoints and controller job logs (GH actions: PRs linked below) to identify the conflicting jobs.
remediation: Short-term: (a) Introduce a lease expiry on soft pins so temporary holds are automatically released after 30s; (b) Add an emergency operator API to force-release pins safely (requires audit logging). Long-term: (a) Implement a global arbitration step for multi-region rollouts that serializes promotion/rollback decisions per model-version across regions; (b) Make health-signal aggregation configurable to use global windowing for multi-region rollouts; (c) Add deadlock detection and automated fallback that will pause new rollout attempts and alert SRE.
action_items: AI-1: Add 30s lease expiry to soft pin implementation and deploy as hotfix (owner: Marcus Chen, estimate: 1).
AI-2: Implement operator API to force-release pins with multi-party audit log (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 3).
AI-3: Add global arbitration lock for cross-region rollouts; prototype as opt-in feature flag (owner: runtime-core, estimate: 8).
AI-4: Update health signal aggregation to support global smoothing window for multi-region rollouts and add tests (owner: telemetry, estimate: 5).
AI-5: Add deadlock detection metric and alert if the same rollout job is retried > N times within T seconds (owner: runtime-scheduling, estimate: 2).
AI-6: Postmortem review with PM and Design to ensure rollout UX surfaces multi-region coordination and expected behavior (owner: Elena Martínez, estimate: 2).
AI-7: Customer communication: send targeted incident summary to affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps (owner: CSM Ops, estimate: 1).
followups: Schedule design review of rollout UX by 2026-03-20 to discuss visible indicators and manual override controls.
Create a chaos test that simulates asynchronous health signals across regions and validates arbitration prevents oscillation.
Audit recent rollouts over last 90 days for signs of transient pin holds exceeding 15s to identify other hotspots.
Coordinate with Dedicated/Dedicated-Customer Success to ensure private deployments receive the hotfix in the next patch window.
postmortem_notes: Operators found log correlation keys inconsistent between controller and pin service which slowed root cause discovery. We will standardize trace IDs across the rollout stack. The incident underscores that multi-region rollouts expose weak global invariants; until global arbitration is in place multi-region rollouts will be gated by policy for high-impact models.
